title: Seven Trees, One Arrow: Then Nothing
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.instagram:
One arrow pierced seven trees. Yet in the first duel, Rama's arrow never flew.

Rama's single arrow pierced seven sala trees, a mountain and the earth (Valmiki Ramayana 4.12.3). Yet in Sugriva's first duel with Vali, the arrow never flew. Rama's reason: "By voice, radiance, gaze, prowess and words, I see no difference between you two" (4.12.31). The answer was a flowering creeper around Sugriva's neck.

Did you know the brothers looked identical?

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

Verses:
• Rama raised his bow and loosed a single arrow. It pierced seven sala trees, the mountain and the earth, and returned to his quiver. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.1-4.12.4
• "My lord, today itself, kill Vali, my enemy in the form of a brother." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.11
• They all reached Kishkindha and hid among the dense trees. Sugriva roared, and Vali burst out in fury. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.14-4.12.16
• The two brothers fought with fists like thunderbolts. Rama stood with his bow drawn. But the arrow never flew. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.17-4.12.20
• "You told me: challenge him. If you never meant to kill Vali, you should have said so then, my lord." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.26-4.12.27
• "Sugriva, my friend, let go of your anger. In dress, in build, in gait, in voice, I saw no difference between you two." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.29-4.12.32
• Rama said: "Lakshmana, uproot this flowering gajapushpi creeper and put it around Sugriva's neck." Lakshmana did. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.34-4.12.37

claims.claim: Rama raised his bow and loosed a single arrow. It pierced seven sala trees, the mountain and the earth, and returned to his quiver.
"My lord, today itself, kill Vali, my enemy in the form of a brother."
They all reached Kishkindha and hid among the dense trees. Sugriva roared, and Vali burst out in fury.
The two brothers fought with fists like thunderbolts. Rama stood with his bow drawn. But the arrow never flew.
"You told me: challenge him. If you never meant to kill Vali, you should have said so then, my lord."
"Sugriva, my friend, let go of your anger. In dress, in build, in gait, in voice, I saw no difference between you two."
Rama said: "Lakshmana, uproot this flowering gajapushpi creeper and put it around Sugriva's neck." Lakshmana did.

verify_note: Every line cites CE Kishkindha; character lines are close Hindi renderings of the cited verses. Vali's line 'what merit...' is 4.17.13; Rama's hunting answer is 4.18.34-36.
